format: FLAC, 24-bit, 48 kHz; stereo where the brief asked for it, otherwise mono
finish: 48 kHz (soxr VHQ); onset trimmed (3 ms before the first 1 ms frame within 40 dB of the peak, held in 3 of 10 frames), 2 ms de-click; peak -1 dBFS; raised-cosine fade-out; FLAC 24-bit. Where a bright transient's inter-sample peak would pass full scale, the gain is set by the true peak instead (ring_lift). Loop-safe beds are not faded. hall_impulse is unit-energy, not peak-normalised.
earshot_rule: pass = the description beats every alternative in earshot's forced choice (p_vs_alts) and is 'strong' (z >= 3 among earshot's vocabulary) or holds at least 60% of the choice and 2x the best alternative (sound.md section 4). A fail is evidence, not a veto: the ear decides.

how.detail: three decaying partials, each a doublet that beats slowly (hum 47.93 Hz, T60 20 s, split 0.21 Hz; prime 95.85 Hz, T60 17 s, split 0.34 Hz; 191.7 Hz at -12 dB, T60 11 s), the two halves of each doublet panned slightly apart; a soft strike (a sine falling 150 to 60 Hz in 75 ms and a breath of noise under 380 Hz); 1.5 s fade-out; peak -1 dBFS

sounds.licence: original synthesis (numpy, this script); no third-party material
sounds.caveat: All of its energy is under 200 Hz: phone and laptop speakers will play almost none of it, so judge it on full-range speakers or headphones. The film stroke itself has partials at 83 and 110 Hz that sit 13-14 Hz either side of this body's 95.9 Hz prime and may beat against it: if the low end sounds rough, high-pass the film stroke at about 125 Hz and let this file own everything below. Alone it does not read as a bell (it is only a bell's bottom two partials): the test that matters is under the film stroke (earshot.under_film_stroke). It makes the bell read LARGE; it does not stop the film stroke reading as a gong, which comes from the stroke's own upper partials.

sounds.name: hall_impulse
sounds.what: A synthetic cathedral impulse response for a convolution reverb: wet only (no direct sound), 90 ms pre-delay built in, RT60 about 6.3-7.2 s through the middle, dark (pink above 500 Hz, and the top decays faster: 3.6 s at 4 kHz, 2 s at 8 kHz by design), left and right decorrelated.

how.detail: independent Gaussian noise per channel in ten cos^2 octave bands, each with its own exponential decay (design RT60: 31.5 Hz 5.6 s, 63 Hz 6.6 s, 125 Hz 7.2 s, 250 Hz 7.2 s, 500 Hz 6.9 s, 1000 Hz 6.3 s, 2000 Hz 5.2 s, 4000 Hz 3.6 s, 8000 Hz 2.0 s, 16000 Hz 1.1 s); -3 dB an octave above 500 Hz and a gentle low-pass at 9 kHz; a 45 ms build-up; 14 low-passed early reflections over the first 180 ms at -9 dB of the tail; 0.4 s fade-out; unit energy per channel
how.normalisation: unit energy (sum of squares = 1 per channel, mean of the two)

sounds.licence: original synthesis (numpy, this script); no third-party material
sounds.caveat: Normalised to UNIT ENERGY per channel, not to -1 dBFS (its sample peak is about -20 dBFS): a signal convolved with it comes back at roughly its own level, so set the wet gain in the mix (start around -12 to -18 dB under the dry voice). The file is 9 s long, so every convolved sound grows a 9 s tail: leave room at the end of the film. The earshot check is run on a test clap convolved with it (audio/gen/hall_impulse_clap_test.wav), not on the impulse itself.
